section: Right to Freedom - Article 19 (six freedoms) and reasonable restrictions
subsections: Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an essential constitutional condition for an assembly protected under Article 19(1)(b)?
o: It must be confined to private premises
It must consist of at least five persons
It must be approved by the Union Government
It must be peaceful and unarmed
accepted.x: The freedom to assemble under Article 19(1)(b) protects only peaceful and unarmed assemblies. Violent, disorderly or armed assemblies are outside its protection.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact constitutional qualifier and reject broader or substituted conditions.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are included within the freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 19(1)(b)?
1. Meetings
2. Demonstrations
3. Processions
4. Armed gatherings
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Meetings, demonstrations and processions may be protected when peaceful and unarmed. Armed gatherings are excluded from the protection.
accepted.tq: Separate the protected forms of assembly from the disqualifying condition of being armed.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: An assembly held on public land becomes constitutionally unprotected when it is characterised by which of the following?
o: Violence, disorder or possession of arms
Participation by citizens from different States
A demand submitted to the authorities
accepted.x: The protection of assembly does not extend to violent, disorderly or armed assemblies. A political objective or inter-State participation by itself does not remove the protection.
accepted.tq: Apply the limiting words of the right to a practical situation rather than focusing on the purpose of the assembly.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: An assembly of five or more persons may be declared unlawful under which provision as identified in the constitutional law framework?
o: IPC Section 141, corresponding to BNS Section 189
IPC Section 144, corresponding to BNS Section 163
IPC Section 189, corresponding to BNS Section 141
IPC Section 153, corresponding to BNS Section 163
accepted.x: The unlawful-assembly provision referred to is IPC Section 141, corresponding to Section 189 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Section 144 of the IPC and Section 163 of the BNSS concern prohibitory orders.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the provisions on unlawful assembly and those on prohibitory orders.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: Prohibitory orders that were earlier issued under Section 144 of the CrPC are now associated with which provision?
accepted.x: The notes identify Section 163 of the BNSS as the corresponding current provision for prohibitory orders earlier associated with Section 144 of the CrPC.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor-successor pairing to avoid confusing unlawful-assembly provisions with prohibitory-order provisions.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the right to strike:
1. The right to strike is a Fundamental Right under Article 19.
2. The right to strike is treated as a legal right.
3. A gherao is constitutionally protected as an exercise of peaceful assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The right to strike is not a Fundamental Right; it is only a legal right. A gherao is not protected as a peaceful assembly.
accepted.tq: Test the common confusion between a Fundamental Right and an ordinary legal right.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which case is associated with the proposition that a demonstration may be protected but the right to strike is not a Fundamental Right?
o: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Kameshwar Prasad v. State of Bihar
T.K. Rangarajan v. State of Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: Kameshwar Prasad is identified with the distinction that peaceful demonstration may be protected, whereas the right to strike is not a Fundamental Right.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial decision with the specific proposition for which it is cited.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: With reference to government employees, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Their right to strike is protected by Article 21 alone.
They possess an unrestricted Fundamental Right to strike.
They may strike whenever a demonstration is peaceful.
They have no right to strike.
accepted.x: The decision in T.K. Rangarajan (2003) is cited for the proposition that government employees have no right to strike.
accepted.tq: Watch for the authority-specific trap in which a general proposition is incorrectly extended to government employees.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which case is associated with the proposition that bandhs are illegal because they curb the freedoms of other persons?
o: All India Bank Employees' Association case
accepted.x: CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar (1997–98) is cited for holding that bandhs are illegal because they interfere with the freedoms of others.
accepted.tq: Link the named judicial decision to its distinctive holding instead of to the broader right of protest.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: The right to form co-operative societies was added to Article 19(1)(c) by which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Ninety-seventh Amendment Act, 2011 added co-operative societies to the freedom of association under Article 19(1)(c).
accepted.tq: Test the amendment-number and year pairing directly.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Ninety-seventh Amendment, 2011, relating to co-operative societies, is also associated with which provisions?
accepted.x: The amendment relating to co-operative societies is also associated with Article 43B and Part IXB.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure amendment association and match the connected Article and Part.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: The right to protest, though not expressly written as a separate freedom, has been read primarily from which provisions?
accepted.x: The right to protest is read from freedom of speech and expression, peaceful assembly, and the right to life and personal liberty under Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional source provisions rather than looking for a separately named right.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to peaceful protest, consider the following statements:
1. Peaceful protest is recognised as a right of everybody.
2. A protest may occupy public space without restriction because it is peaceful.
3. A protest must not disturb other citizens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Peaceful protest is recognised as a right, but it cannot occupy public space without limitation or trouble other citizens. Therefore, statements 1 and 3 are correct.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement that converts a qualified right into an unrestricted one.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Centre has defended restrictions under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act in relation to associations by invoking which provision?
accepted.x: The Centre has invoked Article 19(4), which concerns reasonable restrictions on the freedom to form associations or unions, in defending FCRA curbs.
accepted.tq: Match the restriction clause with the corresponding freedom under Article 19.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: What was the specific scope of the restriction associated with the INSAF judgment concerning foreign funds?
o: It barred only registered co-operative societies from receiving foreign funds.
It barred all associations from receiving foreign funds.
It removed all restrictions on associations receiving foreign funds.
It barred only bodies in active politics from receiving foreign funds.
accepted.x: The INSAF judgment is identified as barring only associations involved in active politics from receiving foreign funds, not all associations.
accepted.tq: Watch the scope words “only” and “all” when distinguishing a limited judicial holding from a blanket prohibition.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of assembly and association - limits (gherao, strikes, arms), co-operatives  [other exams]

accepted.s: Article 19(1)(d) and Article 19(1)(e) respectively guarantee freedom of:
accepted.x: Article 19(1)(d) guarantees movement throughout India, while Article 19(1)(e) guarantees residence and settlement in any part of India.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent clauses by fixing the d–e sequence before considering the options.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of movement and residence - restrictions for Scheduled Tribes

accepted.s: Restrictions on the freedoms under Articles 19(1)(d) and 19(1)(e) may be imposed in the interests of:
o: Only the economic interests of the Union
The general public and the protection of Scheduled Tribes
Only the customs of urban residents
accepted.x: Article 19(5) permits reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public and for protecting the interests of Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Identify both limbs of the constitutional restriction instead of selecting a single-purpose option.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of movement and residence - restrictions for Scheduled Tribes

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of a restriction under Article 19(5)?
o: Suspending freedom of speech during every public emergency
Prohibiting all citizens from changing their profession
Preventing all demonstrations on private land
Limiting outsiders' entry and settlement in certain tribal areas
accepted.x: Restrictions on outsiders' entry and settlement in tribal or Inner Line areas may protect Scheduled Tribes' culture and land under Article 19(5).
accepted.tq: Apply the stated constitutional purpose to the concrete example of tribal and Inner Line areas.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of movement and residence - restrictions for Scheduled Tribes

accepted.s: The protection of Scheduled Tribes under Article 19(5), in relation to movement and residence, is primarily intended to safeguard their:
accepted.x: The restriction may be used to protect the culture and property or land interests of Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Match the restriction with the specific protected interest rather than with an unrelated Article 19 freedom.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of movement and residence - restrictions for Scheduled Tribes

accepted.s:
Which of the following is authorised by Article 19(6)?
1. Prescribing professional or technical qualifications
2. Carrying on a trade by the State to the exclusion of citizens
3. Creating a State monopoly in a trade
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Article 19(6) permits the State to prescribe professional or technical qualifications and to carry on a trade to the exclusion of citizens, thereby permitting State monopolies.
accepted.tq: Combine the qualification and State-monopoly limbs instead of treating Article 19(6) as applying to only one of them.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of profession, trade - State monopoly and qualification limits

accepted.s: The power of the State to prescribe professional or technical qualifications and to create a State monopoly under Article 19(6) was inserted by which Amendment?
accepted.x: The relevant provisions of Article 19(6) were inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.tq: Match the Article 19 exception with the amendment that inserted it.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of profession, trade - State monopoly and qualification limits

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT protected as an occupation under the freedom of profession, trade or business?
o: A trade conducted under a State monopoly
A dangerous or immoral trade such as trafficking
A lawful profession subject to reasonable regulation
A trade requiring prescribed technical qualifications
accepted.x: There is no right to carry on dangerous or immoral trades, such as trafficking. Article 19(6) also permits qualifications and State monopolies.
accepted.tq: Find the exception that is inherently outside the protected field rather than merely regulated within it.
accepted.sec: ■ Freedom of profession, trade - State monopoly and qualification limits

accepted.s: Article 358 operates automatically when a National Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of:
o: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
accepted.x: Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 only when the National Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of war or external aggression.
accepted.tq: Fix the emergency grounds and reject the broader but constitutionally incorrect alternatives.
accepted.sec: ■ Suspension of Article 19 during emergency - Article 358 condition

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 358:
1. It suspends Article 19 automatically during a qualifying National Emergency.
2. It applies when the Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion.
3. After the Forty-fourth Amendment, only laws related to the Emergency receive the relevant protection.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Article 358 operates automatically for an Emergency based on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion. The Forty-fourth Amendment also limited protection to laws related to the Emergency.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-based exception to detect the false emergency ground.
accepted.sec: ■ Suspension of Article 19 during emergency - Article 358 condition

accepted.s: For which grounds of National Emergency may Article 359 operate, according to the stated constitutional distinction?
o: War, external aggression and armed rebellion
accepted.x: Article 359 may operate during an Emergency proclaimed on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion, subject to a Presidential order.
accepted.tq: Contrast the three grounds under Article 359 with the narrower grounds under Article 358.
accepted.sec: ■ Suspension of Article 19 during emergency - Article 358 condition

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Provision)
 a. Article 358
 b. Article 359
 c. Article 19(1)(d)
 d. Article 19(6)

List-II (Subject)
 i. Freedom of movement
 ii. State monopoly and professional qualifications
 iii. Automatic suspension of Article 19 in a qualifying Emergency
 iv. Presidential order concerning enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights

option_a: a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii
option_b: a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
option_c: a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
option_d: a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii
accepted.x: Article 358 concerns automatic suspension of Article 19; Article 359 concerns enforcement of specified rights by Presidential order; Article 19(1)(d) concerns movement; and Article 19(6) concerns qualifications and State monopoly.
accepted.tq: Start with the emergency pair and then match the two Article 19 clauses by their subject.
accepted.sec: ■ Suspension of Article 19 during emergency - Article 358 condition

accepted.s: The expression “golden triangle” in constitutional jurisprudence refers to the relationship among:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court's decision in Maneka Gandhi linked Articles 14, 19 and 21 as the constitutional golden triangle.
accepted.tq: Identify the well-known constitutional grouping by its exact Article numbers.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: Which case is associated with linking Articles 14, 19 and 21 as the constitutional “golden triangle”?
accepted.x: Maneka Gandhi (1978) is identified with linking Articles 14, 19 and 21 as the golden triangle.
accepted.tq: Associate the constitutional doctrine with the case that established the cited linkage.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following reflects the Supreme Court's stated position on peaceful and lawful protest?
o: It is available only to associations registered under the Societies Act.
It is limited to strikes by government employees.
It is everybody's right, but it must not occupy public space or trouble citizens.
It is an absolute right that cannot be restricted under Article 19.
accepted.x: The Supreme Court recognised peaceful and lawful protest as everybody's right while emphasising that dissent must not occupy public space or trouble citizens.
accepted.tq: Preserve both the recognition of the right and its public-order limitation.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: In June 2026, the Supreme Court directed the Government to frame guidelines concerning:
accepted.x: The stated current-affairs development concerns a direction to the Government to frame guidelines on online content.
accepted.tq: Match the current judicial direction with its precise subject instead of the neighbouring Article 19 issues.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the debate concerning films and the press under Article 19?
o: The press can be pre-censored, whereas films cannot be pre-censored.
Films can be pre-censored, whereas the press cannot be pre-censored.
Both films and the press may be pre-censored in exactly the same manner.
Neither films nor the press is subject to any restriction.
accepted.x: The stated distinction is that films can be pre-censored, whereas the press cannot be pre-censored.
accepted.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison trap between two forms of expression.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's prohibition of an NCERT chapter on judicial corruption was criticised as censorship primarily under which Article?
accepted.x: The criticism characterised the prohibition of the NCERT chapter as censorship implicating freedom under Article 19.
accepted.tq: Match the current controversy with the Fundamental Right directly implicated by the subject matter.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which developments have been stated to revive the debate on interception of communications?
1. Phone-tapping rulings of the Madhya Pradesh High Court
2. Phone-tapping rulings of the Delhi High Court
3. The amendment relating to co-operative societies
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Phone-tapping rulings of the Madhya Pradesh and Delhi High Courts were stated to revive the interception debate. The co-operative-societies amendment is unrelated to that development.
accepted.tq: Group the two developments belonging to the same current-affairs issue and exclude the unrelated constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles
